title: A Bloom filter, bit by bit
sub: Membership in a fraction of the memory: no false negatives, occasional false positives.
legend: bits for the word being inserted
the deciding 0, or a false positive

frames.caption: A Bloom filter: 16 bits, all 0, and 3 hash functions. It stores no words at all, just bits.
Insert cat: its three hashes are 1, 1, 6. Set those bits to 1.
Insert dog: its three hashes are 8, 5, 7. Set those bits to 1.
Insert owl: its three hashes are 2, 5, 14. Set those bits to 1.
Insert emu: its three hashes are 2, 4, 8. Set those bits to 1.
Insert yak: its three hashes are 12, 4, 2. Set those bits to 1.
Query dog: bits 8, 5, 7 are all 1, so answer "probably yes". Correct.
Query fox: bit 9 is 0, so fox was definitely never inserted. A no is always right.

Query bee, never inserted: bits 5, 7, 7 are all 1, set by other words. Answer "probably yes": a false positive. With more bits per word and the right number of hashes, these get rare: 10 bits per word gives under 1%.
